_std_values: Tag a task with the standards it implements. Keys must match the 'standards' list below.

phases.name: Foundations
phases.summary: PyTorch fundamentals before any agent work: tensors, autograd, nn.Module, training loops.

phases.name: Neural net from scratch
phases.summary: A neuron built with NumPy only: no torch, no autograd. The forward pass, loss and gradients are written by hand.

tasks.title: Train a neuron on the OR gate
Show a single neuron can't learn XOR

phases.name: First agent
phases.summary: A one-week sprint: wrap a language model in a cognitive loop that plans, calls tools, reviews its own errors and adjusts.

tasks.title: Scope, architecture, tool selection, env setup
Core loop: plan → act → observe → review
Error handling and self-review of failed tool calls
Run code-executing tools in a sandbox
Ask for human approval before risky tool calls

phases.name: Multi-agent systems
phases.summary: Split one agent into roles that hand work to each other, then compare our version with a standard framework.

tasks.title: Planner, Researcher, Executor and Reviewer roles
Rebuild the flow in LangGraph or AutoGen and compare
Long-term memory in a vector database

phases.name: Standards, security & ship
phases.summary: Connect the agents through open protocols, lock down what they can do, measure them, and publish.

tasks.title: Expose our tools as an MCP server
Let our agent use existing MCP servers
Agent identity with OAuth access tokens
Deploy a public demo and write up what we learned

evolution.summary: If-then rules, scripts and early RPA. Predictable tasks only, no real decisions.
Intent recognition, voice assistants and chatbots. Answers single questions.
evolution.note: Genesis builds the ML underneath by hand: a neuron, a loss, gradient descent, and why one neuron can't learn XOR.

evolution.summary: LLMs generate text and code and reason through puzzles, but stay reactive and prompt-dependent.
LLMs inside cognitive loops: planning, RAG, tool use, self-review, adjusting until the goal is met.
evolution.note: Awaken is our first agent loop. It is being scoped now.

evolutionEvents.label: Siri
evolutionEvents.text: Apple ships Siri on the iPhone 4S: a voice assistant built on intent recognition.

evolutionEvents.label: GPT-3
evolutionEvents.text: OpenAI's GPT-3 paper shows one large model can do many tasks from a prompt.

evolutionEvents.label: ReAct
evolutionEvents.text: The ReAct paper interleaves reasoning and tool actions in one loop.

evolutionEvents.label: ChatGPT
evolutionEvents.text: ChatGPT brings LLM chat to the public.

evolutionEvents.label: AutoGen
evolutionEvents.text: Microsoft publishes AutoGen for multi-agent conversations.

evolutionEvents.label: MCP
evolutionEvents.text: Anthropic open-sources the Model Context Protocol.

evolutionEvents.label: A2A
evolutionEvents.text: Google announces the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol; it moves to the Linux Foundation in June 2025.

evolutionEvents.label: ACP → A2A
evolutionEvents.text: IBM's Agent Communication Protocol (ACP) merges into A2A under the Linux Foundation.

evolutionEvents.label: MCP → AAIF
evolutionEvents.text: Anthropic donates MCP to the Linux Foundation's new Agentic AI Foundation.

evolutionEvents.label: Our repo
evolutionEvents.text: NJR and SA start building an agent from one neuron up.

steps.title: Pick 2–3 target projects (MCP servers, LangGraph, AutoGen, PyTorch ecosystem)
Read each contributing guide and set the project up locally
Start with docs fixes and good-first-issue labels
Land a first merged PR
Publish Genesis and Awaken as documented open source

plan._shape: Stages are dated blocks of work. Link a stage to a phase (phase id) or an era (era index) and its status follows that item; otherwise set status. Steps run in order.

cadence.what: 30-minute plan: pick this week's steps from this page and split them between NJR and SA.
Work on a branch per step. Commit small, with messages that name the step.
The other person reviews the PR and runs the notebook or demo.
Demo what changed, update task status in progress.json, redeploy the site.

workflow.title: Pick a step
workflow.text: Take the next open step from the current stage on this page.

workflow.title: Branch
workflow.text: Create a branch named after the step, e.g. awaken-tool-schemas.

workflow.title: Build
workflow.text: Work in the stage's folder under Collabe-work/. Comment the why, not just the what.

workflow.title: Review
workflow.text: Open a PR. The other person reviews it and runs it locally.

workflow.title: Merge & mark
workflow.text: Merge, then set the task's status in progress.json to done or progress.

workflow.title: Ship the update
workflow.text: Run vercel --prod from workspace/NJRProjects so this site shows the new status.

stages.title: Close out Genesis

steps.title: SA pushes sa_neuron_from_scratch.ipynb
Compare both notebooks: initialization, learning rate, loss curves
Tick the Genesis README checklist and mark the phase done

stages.exit: Both notebooks are in the repo and the comparison is written up.

stages.title: Finish PyTorch foundations

steps.title: Finish tensors: indexing, broadcasting, reshaping, moving to the mps device
Autograd: requires_grad and backward(), checked against Genesis's hand-written gradients
Rebuild the XOR 2-layer net with nn.Module, nn.Linear and nn.Sigmoid
Loss functions and optimizers: MSE vs BCE, SGD vs Adam on XOR
A reusable train/eval loop on a small real dataset

stages.exit: PyTorch reproduces the Genesis XOR result, and the training loop is a template we can reuse.

stages.title: Awaken sprint: first agent

steps.title: Choose the model (Claude API or a local Ollama model), create agent/, keep API keys in a gitignored .env
Core loop: plan → act → observe → review, with a max-steps limit
2–3 tools defined with JSON schemas: calculator, file reader, our Genesis classifier
Scratchpad memory across steps
Error handling: bad arguments and failed tools are fed back to the model to retry
Run the code tool in Docker, and ask for approval before any file write
End-to-end demo scenario and writeup

stages.exit: One command runs the demo end to end, and the README explains the loop.

stages.title: Multi-agent systems

steps.title: Split Awaken into Planner, Researcher, Executor and Reviewer roles
Shared state and message passing between the roles
Long-term memory in Chroma
Rebuild the same flow in LangGraph and compare code size and reliability
Agent-to-agent messaging over A2A (ACP merged into it)
Joint demo with SA

stages.exit: Our version and the LangGraph version solve the same task, with a written comparison.

stages.title: Standards, security & ship

steps.title: Expose our tools as an MCP server with the Python SDK
Connect our agent to an existing MCP server, such as filesystem or GitHub
Agent identity with an OAuth client-credentials token
Least-privilege permissions for each tool
Evaluation harness in Inspect: 10–20 tasks with a success rate
Public demo and writeup on this site

stages.exit: All 8 standards are at least in progress and the eval score is published.

stages.title: Era 1: Rule-Based Automation

steps.title: Read about if-then systems, expert systems and RPA
Build a 20-line rule-based chatbot and list where it breaks
Write the era note in progress.json

stages.exit: Note written and status set to done.

stages.title: Era 2: Conversational AI & Early ML

steps.title: Read about intent recognition and early assistants like Siri
Train a tiny intent classifier in PyTorch
Write the era note

stages.exit: Note written and status set to done.

stages.title: Era 3: Generative AI

steps.title: Read the GPT-3 paper's introduction and results
Call an LLM with no tools and record what it can't do: memory, actions, fresh data
Write the era note

stages.exit: Note written and status set to done.

stages.title: Era 4: Agentic AI

steps.title: Read the ReAct paper and Building effective agents
Map Awaken's loop to the PDF's planning, RAG, tool use and self-review
Write the era note

stages.exit: Note written and status set to done.

stages.title: Pick projects and set up

steps.title: Shortlist 2–3 projects: an MCP server, LangGraph or AutoGen, the PyTorch ecosystem
Read each CONTRIBUTING guide and run the test suite locally
Find 2–3 good-first-issue or docs issues

stages.exit: Each project builds locally and we each have an issue picked.

stages.title: First contributions

steps.title: Open a docs fix PR
Open a code PR for a good-first-issue
Respond to review and get it merged
Add each one to openSource.contributions

stages.exit: At least one merged PR each.

stages.title: Publish our own work

steps.title: Add a license and a clean README to Genesis and Awaken
Add runnable examples and a requirements file
Announce it on this site

stages.exit: Genesis and Awaken are public, documented and runnable.
